channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Sob o fogo da diplomacia Donroe
item.description: Trump and Milei allegedly participated in a White House-coordinated operation to support Flávio Bolsonaro in Brazil's 2026 elections, acting as high-profile campaign surrogates. Vice President Geraldo Alckmin criticized the foreign interference, stating that presidents should not involve themselves in other countries' elections.

item.title: Lei Maria da Penha completa 20 anos: o que mudou na legislação e por que mulheres ainda continuam morrendo
item.description: The Maria da Penha Law marked its 20th anniversary with significant advances in protecting women, including classifying domestic violence crimes as unconditionally public prosecution, implementing more humanized police procedures, and enabling faster protective measures. Despite these improvements, feminicides in Brazil reached 1,571 cases in 2025—the highest in historical series—highlighting ongoing challenges in law enforcement and gender-based violence prevention. The issue became central in the 2026 electoral campaigns, with Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro emphasizing the fight against feminicide in their speeches.

item.title: Lula desarma pauta-bomba do PT na economia e deve indicar contenção de gastos obrigatórios em programa de governo
item.description: Lula’s economic team successfully neutralized fiscally risky internal PT proposals — such as zero-fare public transport, privatization reversals, and capital controls — removing them from the 2026 government program. The president endorsed explicit mention of spending restraint on mandatory expenditures and reinforced fiscal consolidation signals, aligned with the 2027 LDO, which targets a primary surplus in 2025 and a two-percentage-point-of-GDP fiscal adjustment by 2030. While universalizing full-time schooling (estimated at R$ 170 billion over 10 years) remains a goal, it will be budget-constrained, with the program avoiding detailed targets to preserve flexibility for electoral and governance phases.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro vai gravar vídeos específicos para diferentes grupos de evangélicos
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro's (PL) campaign is producing customized videos for different evangelical denominations, using specific greetings and themes to appeal to each group, after a Quaest poll showed a technical tie with Lula (PT) among evangelical voters (35% vs 28%, 4-point margin of error). The effort includes meetings with leaders from churches such as Ministério de Madureira, Igreja Universal do Reino de Deus, and Igreja Mundial do Poder de Deus, aiming to strengthen support in a segment where Bolsonaro previously led in July (39% vs 26%).

item.title: O bloqueio das contas de ex-ministro de Bolsonaro
item.description: Former minister Fábio Faria had his bank accounts blocked by the TSE for failing to pay a 30,000-real fine, now updated to 52,000 reais, for distorting a statement by then-candidate Lula during a 2023 debate. He was sanctioned in the same case that also punished Senator Flávio Bolsonaro and Deputy Bia Kicis, who have already paid their fines. The account seizure and inclusion in the federal public sector’s delinquent credit registry followed his March edict summons and non-payment.

item.title: Crusoé: Flávio aponta os responsáveis pela escolha de um vice homem
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) blamed the Centrão bloc for the selection of a male running mate in the presidential ticket, despite his preference for a female candidate. He pointed to Deputy Alfredo Gaspar, rapporteur of the INSS CPMI and pre-candidate for Senate in Alagoas, as the chosen vice-presidential nominee. The statement was made in an interview with Crusoé and republished by O Antagonista.

item.title: Alfredo Gaspar supera 100 mil buscas no Google após ser anunciado como vice de Flávio Bolsonaro, aponta levantamento
item.description: Alfredo Gaspar, federal deputy from PL-Alagoas, surpassed 100,000 Google Brazil searches within 24 hours after being announced as the vice-presidential candidate on Flávio Bolsonaro’s (PL-RJ) ticket for the 2026 elections. The surge in public interest highlights the political impact of the Bolsonaro-aligned coalition’s formation on the electoral agenda.

item.title: Um plano do PT para evitar fiasco com Lula em estádio
item.description: The PT is planning to mobilize supporters from other states, including Minas Gerais, Rio de Janeiro and Paraná, to attend Lula's campaign launch event at the 1º de Maio stadium in São Bernardo do Campo (SP), fearing low turnout. The venue is considered Lula's political birthplace, but there are concerns about initial attendance for the campaign.

item.title: Lula resgata velha estratégia para tentar se afastar do escândalo de lobby de Lulinha
item.description: President Lula reportedly feels betrayed by PT ministers who initially denied knowledge of his son Fábio Luís Lula da Silva’s (Lulinha) lobbying activities in government ministries. According to allies, Lula now believes the aides lied when they claimed they did not assist Lulinha in business dealings. His defense strategy remains unchanged: asserting ignorance of his son’s actions, repeating a pattern seen in past scandals.

item.title: Flávio ataca Lula por Milei e tenta abafar fiasco do vice
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro issued a manifesto opposing the Lula government's decision to downgrade diplomatic relations with Argentina, aiming to divert attention from the failure in selecting Alfredo Gaspar as his running mate. The move was analyzed as a tactical effort to create a 'smokescreen' to overshadow the PL's isolation, lack of Centrão support, and backlash over Gaspar's nomination, which also advances Arthur Lira's local interests in Alagoas.

item.title: Governo tenta reduzir tensão da PF com gabinete de André Mendonça, mas impasse permanece
item.description: The Brazilian government is attempting to ease tensions between the Federal Police and Supreme Court Minister André Mendonça over information flow in the INSS and Master case investigations. While meetings between the AGU, Justice Minister, and Mendonça have smoothed relations and scheduled a follow-up with PF Director Andrei Rodrigues, Federal Police sources say the core legal impasse remains, as judicial restrictions on investigative progress continue to challenge PF autonomy and could jeopardize the validity of future acts.

item.title: 'Fora da bolha': O GLOBO lança 1º episódio de videocast com análises e bastidores da campanha eleitoral de 2026
item.description: O GLOBO launched the first episode of its weekly videocast 'Fora da Bolha', featuring newsroom journalists analyzing the behind-the-scenes and key themes of the 2026 Brazilian election campaign. The inaugural episode covered the investigation into Marco Aurélio Santana Ribeiro (Marcola), the latest Genial/Quaest poll, Alfredo Gaspar’s designation as Flávio Bolsonaro’s running mate, Donald Trump’s influence on Brazilian politics, and Senator Cleitinho’s shifting stance on running for governor of Minas Gerais.

item.title: Os bastidores da despedida de Marcola da campanha de Lula
item.description: Marco Aurélio Santana Ribeiro, known as Marcola, resigned from Lula’s campaign after being questioned about a R$249,000 payment received from lobbyist Roberta Luchsinger. Before stepping down, he called President Lula and PT national president Edinho Silva, blaming internal party conflicts — describing them as 'friendly fire' — for his departure. Lula and Edinho publicly defended him, downplaying the controversy.

item.title: Frase do dia
item.description: Fernando Haddad criticized the selection of Alfredo Gaspar as vice on Flávio Bolsonaro’s ticket, calling it one of the worst choices imaginable and questioning the audacity of appointing someone so unqualified to the position.

item.title: Tarcísio coloca ‘prosperidade’ como eixo central de plano de governo para a reeleição
item.description: Governor Tarcísio de Freitas (Republicanos) has made 'prosperity' the central theme of his 2026 re-election government plan, centered around the SuperAção program, which currently supports 105,000 families and aims to expand to 200,000 by 2027. The plan, featuring ten strategic objectives including security, health, and education, will be filed with the TSE on July 7 and detailed on August 15. Tarcísio has revised his stance on privatizations, stating that private management does not always outperform the public sector, citing the temporary reassumption of CPTM operations after repeated failures by Trivia Trens, including service suspensions and a train fire.

item.title: Aliado de vice de Haddad vai a jantar de chefe do partido de Tarcísio
item.description: Anderson Pomini, an ally of Haddad's running mate Márcio França, attended a dinner hosted by Marcos Pereira, national president of the Republicanos party and supporter of Tarcísio de Freitas. The gathering included business leaders, particularly from the Arab community, at a Lebanese restaurant near Congonhas Airport. Pomini’s presence, appointed by França to lead the Santos Port Authority, highlights political alignments between PT allies and Republicanos, despite the party’s neutral stance in the first round of the presidential election.

item.title: Por que o debate sobre as urnas eletrônicas virou tabu?
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro reignited the debate on Brazil's electronic voting machines during a meeting with diplomats, reviving a discussion that has persisted for 30 years. His remarks, made as a PL presidential candidate, intensified polarization around the reliability of the voting system, a recurring and sensitive issue in Brazilian politics.

item.title: Quaest: 55% prevê vitória de Lula; entre bolsonaristas, um em cada quatro
item.description: According to the Quaest poll, 55% of the electorate expects Lula to win the 2026 presidential election, while 28% believe Flávio Bolsonaro will prevail. The 27-point gap between the two candidates reflects a clear advantage for the incumbent president in voter expectations.

item.title: SobeDesce: da Embraer aos Correios
item.description: Eve Air Mobility, Embraer's subsidiary, completed the first flight of its eVTOL aircraft in Melbourne, signaling progress in urban air mobility. Meanwhile, Correios faces a crisis as its Postal Health plan posted a record loss of 844 million reais in 2025. Politically, the Senate deputy leader of Lula's government saw his wife, daughter, and two sisters subjected to PF searches in an INSS fraud investigation, and the judge who succeeded Sergio Moro in the Lava-Jato task force was suspended for two years by the CNJ over illegalities in an operation-related fund.

item.title: A tempestade vem de fora
item.description: The 2026 Brazilian presidential election unfolds amid scandals involving Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro, but will likely be decided by unprecedented geopolitical factors, including tensions with the U.S., Argentina, and global conflicts affecting exports and domestic stability. Despite leading in polls, both face unprecedented rejection, suggesting the winner will be the 'least hated'.

item.title: Revogação de visto de embaixadora brasileira nos EUA ajuda a escalar a crise política entre países
item.description: The revocation of Brazilian Ambassador Maria Luiza Viotti's U.S. visa, in retaliation for Brazil's alleged delay in accepting the new U.S. ambassador Daniel Perez, has deepened the diplomatic crisis between the two nations. The Lula government denounced the move as arbitrary and politically motivated, linking it to the Trump administration's strategy of pressuring Brazil over its electronic voting system and supporting far-right candidates across Latin America.

item.title: Sport desafia força do Vila Nova como mandante na Série B; veja odds
item.description: Vila Nova hosts Sport in the 21st round of the Série B as an unbeaten home team, with seven wins and two draws in nine home matches in the 2026 Brazilian Championship. Sport aims to end a nine-game winless streak, having drawn their last four. Odds favor Vila Nova (1.88), with a draw at 3.25 and a Sport win at 4.40.

item.title: Campanha eleitoral começa em meio ao silêncio de Lula e Flávio sobre crise fiscal
item.description: The 2026 electoral campaign began with Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro avoiding discussion of the fiscal crisis, despite it being the greatest challenge for the next government. Lula, in launching his re-election bid, focused on symbolic and social themes, while Flávio retreated from spending-cut proposals after negative backlash. Public debt has already reached 82% of GDP and may rise to 87% by 2029, according to the National Treasury.

item.title: Preso e condenado, Jair Bolsonaro é solução e problema para a campanha do filho
item.description: Despite being imprisoned and sentenced to 27 years, Jair Bolsonaro remains the central figure in his son Flávio Bolsonaro’s presidential campaign, directing alliances, selecting candidates, and shaping the candidate’s image and rhetoric. Yet, his use of AI-generated speeches and the STF’s ban on political communication have exposed the campaign to electoral investigations, making him both a key asset and a legal liability for the PL ticket.

item.title: PT pede ao TSE retirada do ar de conteúdo de site ligado ao PL que fornece material a apoiadores
item.description: The PT filed a representation with the TSE requesting the removal of content from the Direita Já website, linked to the PL, alleging it spreads disinformation against Lula and allies, including deep fakes and unfounded accusations. The party claims the site acts as a 'hub' for political content, publishing up to 50 posts weekly, and operates a 'creators' program that pays influencers to disseminate such material. The PT also requests an investigation into whether public party funds are being illegally used to finance these activities.

item.title: Solidão eleitoral
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro attempts to lead the fragmented right in the 2026 elections, but his candidacy remains heavily dependent on his father Jair Bolsonaro’s legacy, lacking original proposals or political autonomy. Despite being the leading opposition candidate in polls, he faces criticism for immaturity, lack of independent vision, and inability to govern effectively, being perceived as a tutelade continuation of the Bolsonaro clan. Researchers note that while the desire for change persists among right-wing voters, Flávio has failed to demonstrate himself as a secure, concrete, or autonomous alternative.

item.title: A sondagem de Valdemar Costa Neto a Michelle Bolsonaro para vice de Flávio
item.description: Valdemar Costa Neto, national president of the PL, reportedly approached Michelle Bolsonaro about running as vice president on Flávio Bolsonaro's 2026 ticket. The idea was abandoned, and the spot went to federal deputy Alfredo Gaspar (PL-AL), announced last Wednesday (5). Allies expressed disappointment, as they had hoped a female running mate would mitigate Flávio Bolsonaro's unpopularity among women voters.

item.title: Eleição apertada?
item.description: A Noblat blog poll shows 31.5% of readers believe the 2026 presidential election will be as close or closer than 2022, while 68.5% disagree. The content also notes Malafaia criticizing Flávio's running mate but admitting support due to lack of alternatives, plus articles on climate, aviation, and PF-STF tensions.

item.title: Vice de Flávio, Alfredo Gaspar não anima o agro
item.description: The selection of Alfredo Gaspar (PL-AL) as Flávio Bolsonaro's (PL-RJ) running mate in the 2026 presidential election surprised the agribusiness sector, which had expected a candidate with stronger ties to rural interests, such as Senator Tereza Cristina. Agribusiness leaders say Gaspar has limited engagement with agricultural policies, focusing instead on public security, and view the pick as a missed opportunity to broaden the ticket's electoral appeal.

item.title: Governo corre para evitar derrota na MP do fim da "taxa das blusinhas"
item.description: The Lula government is racing to approve the measure provisory that ends the so-called 'tax on little blouses' before it expires on September 8, pressuring Senate President Davi Alcolumbre to install the required joint committee for voting. The timeline is tight due to the reduced congressional schedule during the election campaign, with only two concentrated voting windows in August and early September. Senate government leader Teresa Leitão has already spoken with Alcolumbre to warn him of the risk of the MP lapsing.

item.title: Trump prefere guerra ideológica com Brasil a interesse estratégico dos EUA no país, diz analista
item.description: Analyst Anthony Pereira argues that Donald Trump is prioritizing an ideological war against Brazil over U.S. strategic interests in the country, exacerbating tensions with the Lula government. He warns that the influence of figures like Trump and Javier Milei is deepening regional polarization, posing serious risks to Brazilian democracy ahead of the 2026 elections. Pereira cautions that this dynamic could empower authoritarian forces and undermine democratic institutions in Brazil.

item.title: Marcola e Lulinha: campanha de Lula tem semana de crise e mede impacto
item.description: Lula's campaign faces crisis after revelations that advisor Marcola received R$ 249,000 from lobbyist Roberta Luchsinger, who claims it was a private loan. Marcola stepped down to avoid further damage, while PF investigations against Lulinha, the president's son, continue with three STF-authorized inquiries into suspected influence peddling. Allies are divided on electoral impact, with some downplaying the episode and others viewing it as unnecessary damage.

item.title: Haddad quer paternidade da Carbono Oculto e mira despesas de Tarcísio
item.description: Fernando Haddad (PT) will unveil his public security plan this Saturday, claiming 'paternity' of the Carbono Oculto operation and criticizing Tarcísio de Freitas for increasing police lethality without reducing organized crime. The campaign will also challenge what it deems unnecessary state expenditures, including the R$ 3.7 billion advance for Metro Line 6, R$ 2.5 billion paid to highway concessionaires for pandemic-related losses, and the no-bid Muralha Paulista security technology contract.

item.title: Malafaia critica vice de Flávio, mas admite apoio por falta de opção
item.description: Pastor Silas Malafaia criticized the selection of Alfredo Gaspar as Flávio Bolsonaro's running mate for breaking the promise to name a woman and for involving the candidate in a suspected rape of a minor case now under review by the STF. Despite the legal controversies and ally discomfort, Malafaia admitted he will support the ticket due to lack of viable alternatives on the right, as polls show conservative voters are regrouping around Flávio to face Lula in a potential runoff.

item.title: Prefeito ameaça demitir servidores que não votarem em Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: The mayor of Campestre do Maranhão, Fernando Bermuda (PSB), threatened to dismiss municipal employees who do not support Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) in the 2026 elections, using WhatsApp messages and a religious gathering to pressure voters. He stated that those who vote for Lula will be 'on the street' and promoted an AI-generated song linking job retention to support for the Bolsonaro candidate. Employees reported the behavior is recurrent, based on threats and ignorance.

item.title: Governo Lula vê influência de Trump em crise com Milei e Argentina
item.description: The Lula government believes the diplomatic crisis with Argentina, sparked by Javier Milei’s criticisms of Brazil, is part of a U.S. strategy to influence Brazil’s 2026 elections. The tension with Buenos Aires, which led to a downgrade in diplomatic relations, coincides with friction with Paraguay and is seen as part of a broader U.S. effort to pressure Brazil through regional allies aligned with Trump.

item.title: Áudios de Luchsinger para ex-empregada mostram convívio com Lulinha
item.description: Audio messages obtained in the labor lawsuit filed by former domestic worker Zildeni Gomes reveal that Fábio Luís Lula da Silva, known as Lulinha, frequently visited the Brasília residence of lobbyist Roberta Luchsinger, including using the children's bedroom for guests. The messages, attached to the case, indicate daily interaction and refer to Lulinha as the 'little friend' of the former employee. The case is connected to STF investigations into alleged influence peddling involving both individuals.

item.title: Entenda os pontos de atrito entre Mendonça e PF nas investigações sobre fraudes no INSS e o banco Master
item.description: Supreme Court Justice André Mendonça, rapporteur of investigations into fraud at INSS and Banco Master, expressed concern about the Federal Police's independence, stating the probes could affect President Lula’s campaign. The meeting with the Justice Minister occurred the same day 27 PF superintendents issued a public note defending Director-General Andrei Rodrigues, revealing institutional strain.

item.title: Sem ligação de Flávio, voo de madrugada e candidatura de fachada: os bastidores da escolha de última hora de Gaspar como vice
item.description: Alfredo Gaspar was acclaimed as the PL Senate candidate in Alagoas, but had already accepted hours earlier to be Flávio Bolsonaro’s vice-presidential running mate, without final confirmation. The negotiation was conducted in secrecy by Rogério Marinho, Flávio’s campaign coordinator, who instructed Gaspar not to reveal the change even to his family. Despite delivering a Senate-focused speech, Gaspar flew to Brasília unaware if Flávio would choose him — and the presidential candidate never called.

item.title: João Paulo Cunha volta à política 750% mais rico. Jean Wyllys, 80% mais pobre
item.description: Former deputy João Paulo Cunha (PT), convicted in 2012 for passive corruption and money laundering, returns to politics with assets up 750% since then, rising from R$375,000 to R$3.1 million, largely due to a Brasília property. His running mate, Jean Wyllys (PT), saw an 80% drop in declared assets, falling from R$1.2 million to R$250,000. Singer Netinho de Paula (MDB) also re-enters politics with modest assets of R$50,700, far below his performance fee.

item.title: Aliados de Lula querem usar Datena para atacar Flávio na TV
item.description: Allies of President Lula proposed using TV presenter José Luiz Datena as a central figure in the Workers' Party's electoral broadcasts to attack Senator Flávio Bolsonaro, leveraging Datena's credibility from police programs to expose allegations, such as Flávio's alleged ties to banker Daniel Vorcaro of Banco Master. The idea serves as a counter to Flávio's campaign strategy, which plans to deploy his running mate, deputy Alfredo Gaspar, to attack Lula's allies, including Lulinha, Frei Chico, and Marcola. Datena, who left EBC in June to run for federal deputy under the PSB of São Paulo, would be used to lend weight to accusations against Flávio on television.

item.title: Advogado vai ao TSE contra o PL e diz ter sido impedido de concorrer à Presidência
item.description: Lawyer José Adailton Miranda Cavalcante claimed he was blocked from running for president by the PL after the party administratively denied his affiliation, despite his online registration in April 2026. He filed actions with the TSE, including a writ of security, which was rejected by Ministers Kassio Nunes Marques and Dias Toffoli, who argued that electoral justice cannot intervene in internal party matters without direct electoral effects. Cavalcante sought to be included in the pre-candidate list to compete on 'equal footing' with Flávio Bolsonaro, chosen at the PL’s national convention on July 27, 2026.

item.title: Campanha de Flávio monta defesa sobre Gaspar, e aliados de Lula preveem ofensiva sobre vice após fim do prazo de registro
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro’s campaign activated legal and political defenses to mitigate damage from rape allegations against his running mate, Alfredo Gaspar, who denies the claims. The PL chose to confront the issue head-on, pushing for a DNA test to resolve the matter before campaigning begins. The PT plans to exploit the controversy only after August 15, the candidate registration deadline, to avoid interfering with the Bolsonaro ticket’s launch.

item.title: Simone Mendes, Titãs e mais: o que fazer no DF neste fim de semana
item.description: The second weekend of August in Brasília features a diverse cultural agenda, highlighted by the Na Praia music festival with Titãs, Os Paralamas do Sucesso, and Nando Reis on Friday, and Simone Mendes and Filho do Piseiro on Saturday. On Sunday, the free Forreggae 2026 Festival takes place at Praça do Cine Itapuã in Gama, headlined by Mato Seco, blending reggae, forró, and DJ sets. Additional events include theater performances, pagode gatherings, and music tours across the Federal District.

item.title: México estrecha los lazos con Brasil en plena escalada de la tensión entre Lula y Trump
item.description: Mexico's Foreign Minister Roberto Velasco visited Brasília to co-chair the VI Meeting of the Mexico-Brazil Binational Commission, amid growing isolation of both countries due to Donald Trump's influence across the Americas. The meeting takes place at a sensitive time for President Lula, who faces heightened tensions with the U.S. following the cancellation of the Brazilian ambassador's visa and is preparing for re-election in 2026.

item.title: De quem é a culpa do gasto de R$ 1,2 trilhão com juros da dívida?
item.description: President Lula advocates for a 'fiscal seriousness' policy to lower interest rates, but criticizes current fiscal rules that limit public spending, arguing they hinder federal government investments. He questions whether the responsibility for the R$1.2 trillion in interest payments on the debt lies with restrictive fiscal rules or the need for greater public investment to stimulate the economy.

item.title: Autossuficiência dos 'superpartidos' deturpa relação entre Poderes
item.description: The financial self-sufficiency of Brazilian parties, driven by parliamentary amendments and billion-dollar party and electoral funds, is disrupting the balance of power among government branches, reducing parties' reliance on public support and increasing their autonomy and detachment from voters. This trend — evident even in the lack of engagement by traditional parties in the presidential campaign — signals an unprecedented concentration of party power in Brazilian history, posing risks to democratic integrity and the entrenchment of clientelistic structures.

item.title: Registro de Jair Renan Bolsonaro no TSE não informa orientação sexual
item.description: Jair Renan Bolsonaro, federal deputy candidate from Santa Catarina, did not disclose his sexual orientation in his TSE candidacy registration, despite declaring himself heterosexual in 2024. The TSE allows candidates to choose whether to disclose sexual orientation, and currently 44.23% of the 8,229 registered candidacies have opted not to disclose it. His registration also confirms he is a cisgender man and single.

item.title: Doce Maravilha 2026: veja os horários de todos os shows do festival
item.description: The Doce Maravilha 2026 festival takes place from August 7 to 9 at the Jockey Club Brasileiro in Gávea, featuring performances by artists such as Caetano Veloso and Emicida, Paulinho da Viola and Maria Bethânia, Djavan and Leci Brandão. Gates open at 5 PM on Friday and 2 PM on Saturday and Sunday, with ticket prices ranging from R$ 218.40 to R$ 515.97. The schedule includes shows across three stages (Bradesco, Corona, and Deezer) with detailed timing for each day.

item.title: Eleições 2026: Com que idade é obrigatório votar?
item.description: In Brazil, voting is mandatory for literate citizens aged 18 to 70. For those aged 16–17, over 70, and illiterate individuals of any age, voting is optional. Failure to vote when required may result in fines or restrictions on obtaining passports, public employment, or participating in public contests.
